Promotion (promoteHolds, the PutIssue at :1147) keeps the Dispatch chain a root queued with. Since #2273, line() takes an answered awaiting_person root and Waiting applies the ancestry hold to it, so an answered root whose leftover chain names a key that has since become live is dropped from the line until the root's next observation (normally the echo of promotion's in_progress write) clears the chain. Reproduced on Waiting with an answered root carrying Ancestry [LEGION-1] and LEGION-1 in the line: Waiting returns [LEGION-1] only. This contradicts Waiting's own doc ('a root that ran ... records no chain, so the hold never takes an answered root out of the line'). Fix: candidate.Ancestry = nil before that PutIssue; the root has a tree lifecycle from here on, so this is what workflow.Engine.Ancestry would compute.
